title.narrative: Integrated multi-sector support for conflict-affected IDP returnees and host communities in Guto Gida and Haro Limu woreda East Wollega zone, Oromia Region

description.narrative: ltpgt ltbrgtThis project proposal is based on the first standard allocation from UNOCHA, 2025, with the project code CBPF-ETH-25-S-NGO-36125. The goal of the project is to address the humanitarian needs of conflict-affected IDPs through a multi-sectoral response that includes WASH and Nutrition, in Gutu Gida Woreda and Education in Haro Limu woreda of East Wollega Zone, Oromia region.ltbrgtBased on the MIRA Report 2023, The conflict in the Wollegas zone is the leading cause of displacement and other human rights violations. the East Wollega Zone, particularly Gutu Gida and Haro Limu Woredas, is experiencing significant humanitarian needs in various sectors including Nutrition, WASH and Education. Notably, 71% Can’t afford medical fees and Lack medicine (72%) in addition to Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) key findings show that 88% of the population in this location observed signs of distress in women, older persons, girls, and persons with disabilities respectively show more signs of distress 9 out of 10 key informants reported to have observed signs of distress among the different populations in their locations. ltbrgtAfter child labor, nutrition is the second most important issue among the top five concerns affecting children (MIRA2023). Furthermore, food shortages brought on by displacement have caused the physical health of females to worsen or become malnourished. Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) among children under five and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) have increased in the woredas as a result of disruptions in the management of acute malnutrition caused by damage to health facilities. Among 14,495 children screened out Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM) is at 33%, SAM is at 9%, MAM is at 24%, and OPD screening results suggest that 11% and 9% of the people in Gutu Gida woreda are moderately and severely underweight, respectively, according to the most current needs assessment by ANE.ltbrgtThe water supply system issues such as insufficient water storage capacity (60%) and lack of available water (54%) in the East Wollega zone especially in Gutu Gida Woreda have been severely disrupted due to the conflict, resulting in 14% of the water supply schemes being non-functional (75). This has led to acute water shortages and increased risks of waterborne diseases for many residents. Schools and health institutions in Gutu Gida currently lack WASH services, meaning they do not have adequate access to water and latrines as per spare standards.ltbrgtfragile recovery. ltbrgtIn Haro Limu Woreda access to education remains highly problematic for both internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host community children in the targeted woredas. Over the past 2–3 years, many schools have ceased functioning, and some remain closed altogether. After displacement, many IDP children dropped out due to a lack of access to scholastic materials and educational inputs. Where schools are operational, overcrowding is a major issue, with a classroom-to-student ratio of 1:97, a desk-to-student ratio of 1:5, and a student-to-books ratio of 1:5 at the primary level. There has been no provision of educational materials for IDP children, and financial constraints on families have further contributed to dropout rates, leading to a marked decline in the quality of education.ltbrgtANE will prioritize the involvement of local communities and organizations with its sub implementing partner Gurmuu development organization which is established in 2005, having robust operational presence and services to grassroots communities in the Oromia region specially in east Wollega zone. Gurmuu’s intervention related to education focuses on: basic education provision, promoting quality education and girls’ enrollment as well as encouraging community participation. To address the needs of all sectors, an estimated budget of 1,000,000 USD is required. The project is expected to take 12 months, with an implementation period from 1 Aug 2025 to July 31 -Apr 2026.ltbrgtlt/pgt
